questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of excessive thirst and increased urination. She denies any recent illnesses, medications or head trauma. Her laboratory tests reveal normal serum sodium and osmolality, but her urine is dilute with low osmolality. A fluid deprivation test is performed, and her urine osmolarity remains low despite an increase in plasma osmolality. However, administration of desmopressin (DDAVP) results in a significant increase in urine osmolarity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
